name: Puri
description: Puri is one of Hinduism's four sacred dhams, anchored by the 12th-century Jagannath Temple and a long Bay of Bengal beach that draws pilgrims and leisure travellers in roughly equal measure. The town is compact, affordable, and relatively easy to navigate, though it can get overwhelmed during Rath Yatra and peak winter season. It suits spiritually-inclined visitors and beach-goers more than adventure seekers.
nearest_airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar (approx. 65 km)

attractions.name: Jagannath Temple
attractions.description: A towering 11th–12th century Kalinga-style temple dedicated to Lord Jagannath, one of the most important pilgrimage sites in Hinduism. Non-Hindus are not permitted inside the main sanctum, so the interior experience is restricted to Hindu visitors only.

attractions.name: Puri Beach
attractions.description: A wide, flat, golden-sand beach stretching several kilometres along the Bay of Bengal, busy with fishing boats, local vendors, and seasonal crowds. The eastern end near the fishing village is more atmospheric; the central stretch near Marine Drive hotels is more touristy and can be littered.

attractions.name: Grand Road (Bada Danda) & Rath Yatra Route
attractions.description: The main processional avenue connecting Jagannath Temple to Gundicha Temple, famous as the route of the annual Rath Yatra chariot festival. Outside festival season it is a lively commercial street worth a walk to understand the town's religious geography.

attractions.name: Gundicha Temple
attractions.description: The 'garden house' or aunt's temple of Lord Jagannath, where the deities reside for seven days during Rath Yatra. It is quieter than the main Jagannath Temple, offers a better sense of Kalinga temple architecture, and is open to all visitors including non-Hindus.

attractions.name: Raghurajpur Heritage Crafts Village
attractions.description: A government-designated crafts village about 14 km from Puri where nearly every household practises Pattachitra painting, palm-leaf engraving, or stone carving. The murals on house exteriors alone make it worth the short detour, and you can watch artisans at work without pressure to buy.

attractions.name: Chilika Lake – Satapada Dolphin Point
attractions.description: Asia's largest coastal lagoon, accessed from Satapada (about 50 km from Puri) by shared motorboat. The main draw is spotting Irrawaddy dolphins in the lake's mouth; bird diversity on the lake is exceptional from November to February. Boat rides are around 1.5–2 hours and can feel rushed in peak season.

attractions.name: Konark Sun Temple
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage 13th-century temple built as a colossal stone chariot, renowned for its erotic carvings and precise astronomical alignments. It is 35 km from Puri and routinely combined in a day trip; the scale and stone-carving quality are genuinely extraordinary.

attractions.name: Sudarshana Crafts Museum
attractions.description: A small but well-curated museum and live workshop complex near the beach showcasing traditional Odisha crafts including filigree silver work, appliqué, and Pattachitra. It is lower-key than Raghurajpur but more convenient for those based on Marine Drive.

attractions.name: Loknath Temple
attractions.description: A Shiva temple set among narrow lanes near the Jagannath complex, heavily patronised by local devotees and largely off the tourist trail. The inner sanctum is a natural subterranean lingam that is partially submerged in water, which is an unusual sight even by Indian temple standards.

attractions.name: Narendra Tank (Narendra Sagar)
attractions.description: A large sacred tank in the heart of Puri town with a small island shrine in the centre, used for the Chandan Yatra boat festival. Outside festival season it is a quiet, photogenic spot that most tourists skip entirely — a genuine hidden-gem pocket of calm in a busy pilgrimage town.
